sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: The movement is rooted in **Dwaita Vedanta** (Dualism) established by **Madhvacharya**, emphasizing the distinction between the individual soul (Jiva) and the Supreme Being (Vishnu).
• **Foundational Principle 2**: The movement utilized **Dasa Sahitya** (devotional literature in Kannada) to democratize religion, making it accessible to the masses beyond the Sanskrit-speaking elite.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: The **Haridasas** (Servants of Hari) acted as social reformers, using 'Kirtanas' and 'Suladis' to critique caste hierarchies and promote 'Hari-Bhakti'.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The movement is divided into two phases: **Vyasa Kuta** (scholarly, Sanskrit-based) and **Dasa Kuta** (mass-oriented, Kannada-based).

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Scholarly, focused on Vedas, Upanishads, and Puranas; centered in Hampi/Vijayanagara.
Preservation of Vedic orthodoxy and philosophical rigor.
Often linked to the intellectual patronage of the Vijayanagara Empire.
Popular, focused on Kannada compositions (Kirtanas); spread across Karnataka.
Democratization of Bhakti; emotional connection through music.
Direct link to the evolution of Carnatic Music (Purandara Dasa).

items.definition: Known as the 'Pitamaha' (Grandfather) of Carnatic Music. He codified the system of teaching Carnatic music (Sarali Varisai) and composed thousands of Devaranamas.
A saint-poet from a non-Brahmin background (Kuruba caste), highlighting the inclusive nature of the movement. Famous for 'Mohana Tarangini'.
Devotional songs composed by Haridasas, serving as the primary vehicle for spreading Vaishnava philosophy among the common people.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Musical Codification**: Purandara Dasa's pedagogical structure remains the foundation of modern Carnatic music training.
• **Social Integration**: The movement bridged the gap between the elite (Sanskrit) and the commoners (Kannada), fostering a unified regional identity.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Historical marginalization of non-Brahmin Haridasas in mainstream historiography.
• **Solutions**: Re-evaluating the movement through the lens of 'Subaltern Studies' to highlight the egalitarian contributions of saints like Kanakadasa.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'PK-V' (Purandara, Kanaka, Vyasa).
• **Decoded Meaning**: P (Purandara Dasa - Music), K (Kanakadasa - Social Equality), V (Vyasa Kuta - Scholarly/Sanskrit).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses Haridasas with Alvars. Remember: Alvars are Tamil Vaishnava saints (7th-9th century), while Haridasas are Kannada Vaishnava saints (13th-17th century).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Socio-Religious Synthesis' to describe how the Haridasa movement integrated Vedic philosophy with regional linguistic identity.

keyTakeaways: The Haridasa movement was the bedrock of the Dwaita philosophy in Karnataka.
Purandara Dasa is the bridge between the Bhakti movement and the formalization of Carnatic music.
The movement was inherently inclusive, allowing saints from diverse social backgrounds to contribute to the Bhakti canon.
